subject: Pilot packaging: upgrade path and add-on bundling for OrchardHealth
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hannah@orchardhealth.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question: mid-pilot tier swap + add-on bundling

Hi Mateo,

Quick question as we're ramping our OrchardHealth pilot next week. We started on the Compact tier but traffic has spiked and two features (document ingestion and high-precision embeddings) are now blocking workflows. Our PMs asked whether we can: 1) upgrade to the Throughput tier mid-pilot without a full contract amendment, and 2) bundle the embedding add-on with a short-term seat increase (2 months) — ideally without paying the full pro-rated higher commit.

We want to avoid a long procurement loop if possible. Can you share the standard upgrade path, any one-time credits you might extend for a pilot bump, and whether feature bundling can be done as an addendum? Attaching our current usage snapshot (pilot_pricing_table.xlsx).

Thanks —
Hannah

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Packaging question: mid-pilot tier swap + add-on bundling

Mateo — thanks for the context. Short version: we can do an in-flight upgrade and a temporary add-on bundle, but the precise economics depend on uplift size. Options we typically offer: 

1) Fast upgrade (recommended when uplift < 2x):
   - Move them to Throughput tier immediately, pro-rate starting day of upgrade.
   - If total annualized commit increases by >= 50% vs original pilot forecast, offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 15% of the incremental 3-month commit (applied as credit on invoice).
   - No retrospective backbilling if we upgrade effective date is agreed in amendment.

2) Short-term add-on + soft commit (recommended when uplift is temporary):
   - Keep Compact tier, add the embedding/doc-ingestion add-on for a fixed 2-month term at a blended add-on rate (example: 0.75x of monthly throughput rate for two months).
   - Charge upfront for the 2-month add-on; include a one-time 10% pilot credit if they commit to a post-pilot evaluation within 60 days.

3) Hybrid (if they plan to keep higher usage):
   - Immediate partial upgrade (throughput baseline bump) + add-on discounted 10% for first 3 months, then re-evaluate.

Pricing guardrails: discounts beyond the above need Revenue Ops sign-off for deals > $75k annualized incremental. Use this template language when sending to customer: 
   "We can execute a simple one‑page amendment to make the change effective immediately. The amendment will specify the new effective date, pro‑rated commit, and a one‑time credit (if eligible) to be applied on the next invoice. No retroactive charges will be applied prior to the effective date."

I'll prepare the numbers if you can confirm the expected uplift (est. peak tokens / embeddings per month). I pulled their HubSpot record and left a note: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

—Ben
Sr. Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question: mid-pilot tier swap + add-on bundling

Agree with Ben's guardrails. A few operational/legal constraints to flag before you propose anything to the customer: 

- SLA/Capacity: If we move them to Throughput and they rely on reserved pools, we need to confirm region availability for the requested start date. If not available, we fallback to best-effort hosted capacity and note potential burst limits in the amendment.
- Credits: we do NOT apply credits retroactively. The credit can only be applied prospectively on invoices after the amendment effective date.
- Amendment language: include an explicit line that the customer accepts the effective date for billing and any limits to reserved capacity. This avoids disputes after trial spikes.
- MSA addendum draft: I prepared a one-page addendum for quick signature — please review/edit and send it to me for countersign. I attached the draft (redwood-addendum-draft.pdf).

If you want, I'll prepare both amendment options (fast upgrade vs short-term add-on) with the exact pro‑rations and credit math once you send me the uplift numbers.

Kimberly Park
Head of Renewals & Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
